Simulating integrated Brownian motion

Source: vignettes/simulating-ibm.Rmd
simulating-ibm.Rmd

The state is ordered as (f′,f)(f',f). For interval length Δ\Delta and derivative diffusion variance rate λ\lambda, its innovation covariance is

λ(ΔΔ2/2Δ2/2Δ3/3). \lambda \begin{pmatrix} \Delta & \Delta^2/2\\ \Delta^2/2 & \Delta^3/3 \end{pmatrix}.

The analytic Cholesky factor used by Stan can be checked directly.

delta <- 0.8
lambda <- 0.4
L <- ibm_transition_cholesky(delta, lambda)
Q <- ibm_transition_covariance(delta, lambda)
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(L %*% t(L), Q)))
Q
##       [,1]       [,2]
## [1,] 0.320 0.12800000
## [2,] 0.128 0.06826667

Constant lambda gives ordinary IBM. Supplying one value per interval gives the locally varying diffusion used by the adaptive model.

t <- c(0, 0.1, 0.7, 2.2, 3)
ordinary <- simulate_ibm(t, lambda = 0.3, seed = 1)
adaptive <- simulate_ibm(t, lambda = c(0.02, 0.02, 1.2, 0.02), seed = 2)

plot(t, adaptive$f, type = "l", xlab = "t", ylab = "f(t)")
